headline: PSX opens week in the red, plummets amid US-Iran Strait of Hormuz escalation
summary: Monday session (intraday): KSE-100 Index lost 2,215.27 points at 10:19am to stand at 180,026.5 (previous close 182,241.77); as of 12:33pm down 1,706.67 points (-0.94%) to 180,535.10; Business Recorder later reported the index shed 2,202.63 points to 180,039.14. Driver: US and Iran exchanged fresh strikes over the Strait of Hormuz, Iran claimed to have closed the strait, oil prices jumped over 4%; across-the-board selling in autos, cement, banks, E&P, OMCs and power, with HUBCO, MARI, OGDC, PSO, SSGC, SNGPL, MCB, MEBL, NBP and UBL trading in the red; refinery sector was the lone positive per Dawn.

headline: Govt unveils new plan to fast track $6 billion refinery upgrade projects
summary: Petroleum Division submitted amendments to the Brownfield Refining Policy 2023 to the Cabinet Committee on Energy: refineries (PARCO, Attock Refinery/ARL, Pakistan Refinery/PRL, National Refinery/NRL, Cnergyico) that sign OGRA Upgrade Agreements within 90 days get a seven-year package - minimum 10% customs/regulatory duty maintained on imported gasoline and diesel for seven years, a 10% deemed duty incentive on locally produced gasoline/diesel, and sales tax exemption on imported plant, machinery, equipment and materials - to unlock nearly $6 billion in upgrades.

headline: PKR strengthens again, hits 195-day winning run vs USD
summary: Rupee added 3.08 paisa in Monday's interbank session to settle at Rs278.02/USD (from Friday's close of Rs278.05), extending a 195-consecutive-day winning streak vs the dollar (cumulative +Rs3.4018, +1.22% over the streak); intraday band Rs278.20-278.00; open market Rs278.80 buy / Rs279.10 sell.

headline: Pakistan car sales jump 39% in FY26
summary: FY26 cumulative car/LCV/van/jeep sales reached 206,436 units, +39.4% YoY vs FY25's 148,042; June 2026 sales 22,741 units (+4.4% YoY, +28.8% MoM), though passenger cars alone fell 12.9% YoY in June (15,378 units) while LCVs/vans/jeeps rose 79.0% YoY (7,363 units); June brand figures cited: Suzuki 7,719 units (Alto 7,239, Every 480, Cultus 439, Swift 1,668), Toyota 2,650 units, Honda 2,594 units, Hyundai 288 units - no PSX-ticker-level breakdown given in the article.

headline: Sazgar produces 2,488 three-wheelers, 2,374 four-wheelers in June 2026
summary: SAZEW June 2026 output: 2,488 three-wheelers produced (3,267 sold) and 2,374 four-wheelers produced (2,720 sold), combined 4,862 units produced vs 5,987 sold; vs May 2026, four-wheeler production +47.5% (sales +69.6%) and three-wheeler production +52.5% (sales +99.7%) - sales outpacing production indicates inventory drawdown.

headline: PSX plunges over 2% intraday as US reimposes naval blockade on Iran
summary: Tuesday intraday, from previous close of 179,927.04/179,927.05 (Monday): Dawn reported KSE-100 at 176,462.15, down 3,464.89 points (-1.93%); Pakistan Observer reported it down 3,733.34 points to 176,193.70 (-2.07%); Business Recorder reported it shedding over 3,600 points in opening minutes to 176,309.50 as of 9:43am, down 3,617.54 points (-2.01%), with index-heavy MARI, OGDC, PPL, HUBCO, MCB, MEBL, NBP and UBL trading in the red across autos, cement, banks, E&P, OMCs and power sectors. Driver: President Trump announced the US is reinstating a naval blockade of Iranian shipping through the Strait of Hormuz effective Jul 14 (CENTCOM cited 4:00pm ET start), plus a 20% fee on cargo transiting the strait; Brent crude +$1.50 to $84.80/bbl (+1.8%), WTI +$1.70 to $79.84/bbl (+2.2%), four-week highs; AKD Securities' Awais Ashraf quoted: 'The decline is broad-based, with cyclical sectors witnessing the sharpest percentage losses amid heightened uncertainty.'

summary: Select Technologies Limited, a Pakistani smartphone and consumer-appliances maker, raised Rs3.02bn via IPO of 88.9m ordinary shares (10% of post-issue paid-up capital); floor price Rs28.00/share, strike price discovered at Rs34.00/share (21% premium over floor) after book-building; issue oversubscribed 3.23x with ~13,000 investors participating (banks, mutual funds, insurers, pension funds, brokerages, HNWIs, retail). Not currently a KSE100/KMI30 universe constituent - logged for macro/primary-market sentiment context only; ticker symbol not confirmed in source reviewed.

headline: Dada Partners advises Nishat Group on Pakistan's largest private cross-border listed-company acquisition (Rafhan Maize)
summary: Nishat Group acquired 73.9% of Rafhan Maize Products Company Limited (RMPL) for approximately PKR 66 billion - 51% bought from majority shareholder Ingredion Incorporated (USA, which retains a strategic minority stake), 20.5% from a minority shareholder, and 2.4% via mandatory public offer - taking Nishat Group's total stake to a super-majority 75.9%; described in the article as the largest private-sector cross-border M&A of a listed Pakistani company, excluding privatizations. Dada Partners (Private) Limited was exclusive financial advisor to Nishat Group; Cornelius, Lane and Mufti (CLM) was legal counsel; Next Capital was Manager to the Offer.

headline: Pakistan retires record Rs4.7tr debt ahead of maturity
summary: Pakistan retired Rs4.7 trillion (approx. $17bn) of public debt ahead of maturity - described as the largest early-retirement liability-management exercise in the country's history; composition 51% owed to SBP, 49% market debt/government securities; Adviser to the Finance Minister Khurram Schehzad called it the 'largest and most sustained liability management operation,' with average maturity of public debt extended from 2.7 years (FY24) to 3.8 years (FY26) - supportive for macro stability and refinancing risk, no direct PSX-ticker impact disclosed.

headline: Textile exports stagnate at $17.9bn in FY26; June exports drop 16.71% YoY
summary: FY26 textile exports totalled $17.93bn, up just 0.26% YoY from $17.88bn in FY25 (Dawn) - 'one of the weakest performances in recent years' - missing the annual export target by $4.87bn, partly attributed to the suspension of trade with Afghanistan (an export market worth nearly $1.5bn); by product, readymade garments +3.87% in value, yarn +12.40%, knitwear -0.88%, cotton cloth -7.55%. Mettis Global's own figures: June 2026 textile exports were $1.27bn, down 16.71% YoY and 22.72% MoM (from $1.64bn in May), with knitwear -19.99%, readymade garments -12.43%, bed wear -23.29%; textile group products were 53.52% of total June exports. No individual company figures disclosed in either source.

headline: Large-Scale Manufacturing grows 5.77pc despite May slump
summary: LSM sector posted 5.77% YoY growth in the first 11 months (Jul-May) of FY26; QIM index 121.65 vs 115.02 in the corresponding prior-year period, though May alone contracted 0.98% YoY (+1.21% MoM vs April). Top contributors to growth: automobiles +1.53pp (production +58.82%), food products +1.36pp (output +7.75%), garments +1.20pp (exports +7.31%), petroleum products +0.78pp (coke and petroleum +10.56%). Detractors: pharmaceuticals -8.07%, iron & steel -7.49%, chemicals -2.64%, fertilizers -2.25%, textiles -0.09% - sector-level aggregate data only, no individual companies named in the source reviewed.

headline: PSX sets Rs925bn target for Jul-Sep 2026
summary: Published 10:14am PKT: PSX issued a revised Jul-Sep 2026 government-securities auction calendar, on the advice of the Debt Management Office (DMO) of the Ministry of Finance, targeting cumulative Rs925bn issuance of Government of Pakistan Hybrid Sukuk (GHS) and Ijarah Sukuk (GIS) - Rs625bn via Variable Rental Rate instruments across five auctions and Rs300bn via Fixed Rental Rate/Fixed Rate Zero Coupon structures across two auctions, tenors from 3-month to 10-year. This is a routine government debt-auction calendar administered via PSX, not a PSX-company revenue or earnings figure.

headline: Pakistan's FY26 import bill climbs 8.15%
summary: Published 10:11am PKT: FY26 import bill totalled $69.76bn (Rs19.59trn), up 8.15% YoY in dollar terms (8.72% in rupee terms) from $64.51bn (Rs18.02trn) in FY25. Breakdown by commodity group: petroleum $16.86bn (+5.76% YoY, largest contributor), food $9.15bn (+11.66%), metal $6.31bn (+12.07%), transport $4.06bn (+66.36%, sharpest growth); textile was the only major category to decline, at $6.46bn (-12.16% YoY).

headline: HBL unveils HBL PayPak UnionPay co-badge debit card; SBP governor hails launch
summary: HBL, described as Pakistan's largest debit-card issuer, launched the HBL PayPak UnionPay Co-Badge Debit Card at a ceremony at HBL Tower, Karachi, on Jul 15, 2026, developed with 1Link-operated PayPak and UnionPay International to combine domestic PayPak acceptance with UnionPay's international network on one card. SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad welcomed the launch as aligned with SBP's Vision 2028 and the 'Cashless Pakistan' agenda; no revenue, fee or volume figures for the card itself disclosed in the sources reviewed - reputational/strategic item for HBL, not caught in the prior checkpoint.

headline: Mobile banking users reach 137 million as digital payments surge
summary: Published 11:01am PKT, citing SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad: mobile banking users reached 137 million; retail digital transactions rose from 6.9bn to nearly 12bn over the past year; active merchants accepting digital payments rose from ~500,000 to over 2 million; remittances received via digital channels rose from 80% to 92%. Sector-wide digital-payments tailwind, no individual bank ticker figures disclosed.

headline: SECP issues final notices in Unity Foods unusual-trading probe; probe tied to separate FIA criminal case over alleged multi-billion-rupee irregularities
summary: SECP issued final notices on Sept 2, 2026 to four individuals - CEO Muhammad Farrukh, Safdar Sajjad, Fehmida Amin and Hina Safdar - requiring them to appear before its Karachi investigation team on Sept 3, 2026, after they neither appeared nor requested rescheduling from an Aug 31 summons, per ProPakistani. The formal SECP investigation (opened June 2, 2026 under Section 139 of the Securities Act 2015) covers alleged unusual/insider trading in Unity Foods Limited (PSX: UNITY) shares; Farrukh is specifically required to explain and provide records on the pledging of UNITY shares with banks. Per search-indexed reporting (ProPakistani, Business Recorder, TechJuice headlines), this SECP probe separately led to an FIA criminal case (around Aug 31, 2026) against Unity Foods' former management over alleged multi-billion-rupee financial irregularities; one search result cited a discrepancy of about Rs44.7bn between published accounts and internal records, not independently confirmed via a directly-fetched primary article this cycle. No PSX trading halt/suspension of UNITY shares reported in sources checked. Logged as impact 5 (severe - fraud/criminal-case allegations, default per desk criteria Rule 10); escalation flagged.
